headline: 18 law officers resign from Attorney General's Office in protest
summary: Seven deputy and 11 assistant attorney generals aligned with Jamaat-e-Islami quit their posts over judiciary and charter implementation issues.
details: Eighteen law officers of the Attorney General's Office resigned simultaneously on Tuesday afternoon. The group includes seven deputy attorney generals (DAGs) and 11 assistant attorney generals (AAGs).
All 18 officers are aligned with Jamaat-e-Islami and were appointed after the fall of the Awami League government in August 2024.

The resignations are a protest against the non-implementation of the July Charter, the state's opposition to a separate judiciary secretariat, and the repeal of the Supreme Court Judge Appointment Ordinance.
DAG Yusuf Ali, who also resigned, stated that they tried to cooperate with the state after the BNP government came to power but found the state opposing the separation of the judiciary.
He further accused the government of failing to implement the spirit of the Liberation War and the July Uprising, leading to the decision to quit.
caption:
18 law officers, including 7 deputy attorney generals, have quit the Attorney General's Office in a simultaneous resignation.

Eighteen law officers of the Attorney General's Office resigned simultaneously on Tuesday afternoon. The group includes seven deputy attorney generals (DAGs) and 11 assistant attorney generals (AAGs).

All 18 officers are aligned with Jamaat-e-Islami and were appointed after the fall of the Awami League government in August 2024.

The resignations are a protest against the non-implementation of the July Charter, the state's opposition to a separate judiciary secretariat, and the repeal of the Supreme Court Judge Appointment Ordinance.

DAG Yusuf Ali, who also resigned, stated that they tried to cooperate with the state after the BNP government came to power but found the state opposing the separation of the judiciary.

He further accused the government of failing to implement the spirit of the Liberation War and the July Uprising, leading to the decision to quit.

Source: bdnews24.com, Jamuna TV, Somoy News

headline_marked: Faridpur [[DB officer withdrawn]] after law student's death in custody
headline: Faridpur DB officer withdrawn after law student's death in custody
summary: Syed Md Alamgir Hossain was removed from his post following the death of 27-year-old Mirza Ishtiaq Ahmed Pranto while in custody.
details: The officer-in-charge of Faridpur Detective Branch’s Sadar Zone, Syed Md Alamgir Hossain, has been withdrawn from his post and attached to Faridpur Police Lines with immediate effect.
The action was taken following the death of Mirza Ishtiaq Ahmed Pranto, a 27-year-old law student, who died on Sunday while in DB custody.
According to the family, DB personnel detained Ishtiaq on Saturday evening and allegedly assaulted him in front of his mother before he fell ill.
Ishtiaq died at around 8:00 am on Sunday while undergoing treatment at Faridpur Medical College Hospital, still in custody.
Additional Superintendent of Police Fatema Islam stated that the officer's withdrawal was been made on administrative grounds.
The incident sparked protests in Madhukhali, where locals blocked the Dhaka-Khulna highway for about 40 minutes before the funeral.
Local BNP leaders and the Faridpur district unit of the banned Bangladesh Chhatra League have both issued statements demanding accountability or offering condolences.
caption:
A law student died while in DB custody in Faridpur. Now, the officer-in-charge has been withdrawn.

The officer-in-charge of Faridpur Detective Branch’s Sadar Zone, Syed Md Alamgir Hossain, has been withdrawn from his post and attached to Faridpur Police Lines with immediate effect.

The action was taken following the death of Mirza Ishtiaq Ahmed Pranto, a 27-year-old law student, who died on Sunday while in DB custody.

According to the family, DB personnel detained Ishtiaq on Saturday evening and allegedly assaulted him in front of his mother before he fell ill.

Ishtiaq died at around 8:00 am on Sunday while undergoing treatment at Faridpur Medical College Hospital, still in custody.

Additional Superintendent of Police Fatema Islam stated that the officer's withdrawal was been made on administrative grounds.

The incident sparked protests in Madhukhali, where locals blocked the Dhaka-Khulna highway for about 40 minutes before the funeral.

Local BNP leaders and the Faridpur district unit of the banned Bangladesh Chhatra League have both issued statements demanding accountability or offering condolences.

Source: The Daily Star, Prothom Alo
